task: DAEO-clon (W2-112): rewrite §5 of `docs/research/W2-112-shared-reranker.md` to KPI success-7 as the owner re-baselined it (DEC-1048, P-W2-112-F9 (c)); no code changes.
status: DONE. §5 is rewritten and committed as `3559f011f6f0`; only that one file changed.
work_completed: §5 is now titled "The stopgap stays (ACT-RERANK-GPU-SLOTS-1)" and is still the document's last section. It says the module and its `.pth` are **not to be retired by an ACT now** and stay as the machine-wide guard that "caps every reranker, whatever its tree's commit", which is harmless beside W2-112's worker. It explains why in a few sentences (F9: a check holds only while it runs, and old trees come back afterwards through a re-created worktree, an older base checked out for a red check or a bisect, or the old pin kept for rollback). It names the retirement path, P-W2-112-F9 (b): the module is retired only when old code fails closed by construction, in a later ticket, not in W2-112. I removed the two-check precondition, the `rm` commands, the post-removal check, the Undo step and the "why it is safe once the precondition holds" paragraph. I added a read-only check (`cat` the `.pth`, `ls` the module). I kept the rule that the slot lock files are never removed, with its reason. §1's "The stopgap's slots" only says "while the interim module is installed" and never says this ticket retires the module, so it already agreed and I left it unchanged.
files_changed: docs/research/W2-112-shared-reranker.md
evidence: Sandbox check, first: (a) the write failed as required (`OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system: '/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/.sandbox-trial-DAEO-clon'`, and no such file exists afterwards); (b) `git hash-object -w --stdin` worked (printed the object id, exit 0) and `git update-index --refresh` worked (exit 0). Identity: `GOV_ROLE=engineer`, `GOV_TICKET=DAEO-clon`, toplevel `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-112`, branch `w2/W2-112`. `gov.__file__` line: `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-112/src/gov/__init__.py`. Commit `3559f011f6f0` on `w2/W2-112`, 1 file changed, 29 lines added and 51 removed, with trailers `Task: DAEO-clon`, `Role: engineer`, `Implements: DEC-1048,DEC-1033`, `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Hooks folder held only `*.sample` files, and `--no-verify` was not used. After the edit, a search of the file for `rm`, `find "$HOME"`, `Precondition`, `Then, and only then` and `Undo` found nothing (exit 1). §5's new heading: `## 5. The stopgap stays (ACT-RERANK-GPU-SLOTS-1)`. Read refusals: 0. `gov retrieve`: not used. It has no option to skip reranking, and every search tries the shared reranker first, which would break this batch's "run no real reranker, touch no GPU" rule. I read the files the brief names one by one instead and searched only the research document itself. Scratch: `TMPDIR=/tmp/gov-launch-engineer-mh6s0eu5/claude-1000` (the sandbox's own temp folder) held 9 inodes, 28K; `/tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-112` held 2 inodes, 8.0K; the scratchpad held 1 inode, 4.0K. I created no scratch files, so there was nothing to clean up, and all figures are far below the 1 GB / 50,000 limit.
tests: none run (as the brief says, the lead runs `gov accept` after merging the test designer's revision).
discoveries: (1) `governance/project/orchestration/packages/ACT-RERANK-GPU-SLOTS-1.md` §5 (Undo) still says "W2-112's shared reranker replaces it (its ticket then removes these files)". That now contradicts DEC-1048. It is outside my paths, so I did not change it; the CTO or orchestrator should update it. (2) `git status` shows untracked dotfiles in the worktree root (`.bashrc`, `.bash_profile`, `.gitconfig`, `.gitmodules`, `.idea`, `.mcp.json`, `.profile`, `.ripgreprc`, `.vscode`, `.zprofile`, `.zshrc`). I did not create them and they look like sandbox placeholder files; the commit's pathspec left them out.
risks: I could not read the revised `test_w2_112_retirement_act.py` (policy 2 (c)). §5 uses the KPI's wording word for word ("not to be retired by an ACT now", "machine-wide guard", "caps every reranker, whatever its tree's commit", "retired only when old code fails closed by construction", "a later ticket", both lock-file names), but a test that expects other exact phrasing could still fail.
lessons: In this batch `gov retrieve` cannot be run safely, because it always tries the shared reranker first and the reranker uses the GPU. A doc-only brief that forbids touching the GPU should either say retrieval is skipped or give a way to run it without reranking.
proposed_decisions: none
unresolved: The out-of-date "its ticket then removes these files" sentence in ACT-RERANK-GPU-SLOTS-1.md §5 (outside W2-112's paths).
recommended_next_action: The lead merges the test designer's DEC-1048 revision of `test_w2_112_retirement_act.py` and runs `gov accept` on `3559f011f6f0`, then sends W2-112 to the queue.
